title: A stranger texted a photo of your front door — Part 2
style: Warm painterly 2D cartoon illustration, cinematic graphic-novel look: clean bold dark outlines, rich textured digital painting, soft volumetric light, deep warm oranges and moody blues, detailed environment, vertical 9:16 composition.
character: MAIN CHARACTER: a lanky ADULT man drawn as a minimalist cartoon: a perfectly round smooth tan head, two tiny solid black dot eyes set wide apart, short thin eyebrow strokes, a very small simple mouth, no nose, no visible hair, simple long limbs, dark charcoal baseball cap, oversized heather-grey hoodie, black slim pants, white sneakers. Minimal face like a webcomic, not a child, not anime, no big eyes.

scenes.A: Night, the man on the phone in his apartment hallway, worried, standing by his front door with the key in his other hand.
scenes.B: A woman building manager with a flashlight and a ring of keys arriving in the apartment hallway at night, the man beside her, both looking at door 4B.
scenes.C: Two people slowly opening an apartment door marked with a brass plate into a dark room, a strip of warm light inside, suspense.
scenes.D: The lights snapping on in a small apartment full of friends jumping up with party poppers, balloons and a birthday cake with candles, the man frozen in the doorway, joyful chaos.
scenes.E: A smiling young woman with curly hair holding up a phone and laughing, pointing at the man, birthday balloons behind her.
scenes.F: Close-up portrait of the man facing the viewer, laughing in relief, party lights and balloons behind him.

segments.text: You don't go in alone. You call someone.
Your building manager shows up with a flashlight. Together, you walk to 4B.
Your key turns in the lock.
The door swings open. Dark. Then the lights snap on.
Twenty of your friends. A cake. Balloons everywhere.
The unknown number? Your sister's new phone. She rented 4B for one night just for this.
And calling someone first? That was still the right move.
